c1.title: Auth out of the box
c1.description: Google and GitHub OAuth with Auth.js v5. Sessions stored in your own database. No third-party auth service required.

c2.title: Stripe payments
c2.description: Subscription checkout, webhooks, and Customer Portal. Handles upgrades, downgrades, and cancellations automatically.

c3.title: Prisma + PostgreSQL
c3.description: Type-safe database layer with Prisma 7. Works with Neon, Supabase, Railway, or any PostgreSQL provider.

c4.title: Dark mode
c4.description: System-aware dark mode with a toggle. Tailwind 4 CSS variables let you customize your brand colors in one file.

c5.title: Route protection
c5.description: Middleware-based auth guards. Public, auth, dashboard, and admin route groups with zero boilerplate per page.

c6.title: Admin panel
c6.description: User management with role-based access. View all users, their plans, and subscription status in one place.

c7.title: 1-click Vercel deploy
c7.description: Deploy button in the README. From clone to production in under an hour, plus a built-in demo mode to showcase your product, like this site's live demo.

c8.title: Plain Next.js, nothing to learn
c8.description: No compiler step, no config DSL, no proprietary CLI. The App Router, Server Actions and Prisma work as documented, so your Next.js knowledge transfers on day one, and every component stays swappable.

c9.title: Transactional emails
c9.description: Welcome, receipt, and password reset emails via Resend. React Email templates included, branded and responsive.

$kit.title: About {site}
$kit.maintainerBody: . One person, working in the open: the roadmap says what is coming, the changelog says what already shipped, and every release is a tag you can read. Issues and questions are answered by the person who wrote the code.
$kit.noteBody: Tell your story here: what you are building, who it is for, and why it exists. Edit this page in <path>src/app/[locale]/(public)/about/page.tsx</path>.
$kit.what: A complete starting point for a SaaS, not a demo of one. Authentication with OAuth, magic links and passwords. Stripe subscriptions, one-time payments and webhooks whose signature is verified before anything reaches the database. An admin panel with real revenue figures, transactional email, a file-based blog and the marketing site around it. It is the plumbing every product needs and nobody enjoys writing twice, in a codebase small enough to read in an afternoon and yours to change.
$kit.who: People shipping on their own or in a small team, who would rather spend the weekend on the part that makes their product different than on wiring a checkout for the tenth time. It assumes you know Next.js, and that you would rather own the code than rent a platform.

items.question: How do I get started?
items.answer: Create an account, name your first project and you are in. {site} works in the browser, there is nothing to install, and you can invite the rest of your team whenever you are ready.

items.question: How does billing work?
items.answer: You pick a plan and pay by card. Upgrades and downgrades take effect right away and are prorated, invoices land in your inbox automatically, and you can see and change everything from the billing page in your account.

items.question: Who can see my data?
items.answer: You, and the people you invite. Your data lives in our own database rather than being scattered across third parties, card details are held by Stripe and never touch our servers, and we do not sell any of it.

items.question: What exactly do I get?
items.answer: You get a production-ready Next.js 16 codebase with Auth.js, Stripe, Prisma, and Tailwind pre-configured. Clone the repo, set your env variables, and deploy. Everything works out of the box.

items.question: Why not ShipFast or Makerkit?
items.answer: {site} uses a best-of-breed stack where every component is independent. No Supabase lock-in, no proprietary auth layer. If a dependency releases a breaking change, you update one package, not the entire stack.

items.question: Which database providers are supported?
items.answer: Any PostgreSQL provider: Neon (recommended, cheapest), Supabase, Railway, PlanetScale (via Postgres mode), or self-hosted. Just set your DATABASE_URL and run the migration.

items.question: Do I need a Stripe account?
items.answer: Yes. Stripe is used for subscription payments. You'll need to create products and prices in your Stripe dashboard and add the price IDs to your env vars. The setup guide covers this step by step.

items.question: Can I use this for client projects?
items.answer: Yes, MIT license. Use it for as many projects as you want, including client work. No per-project fees.

items.question: What if I need help or find a bug?
items.answer: Open an issue on GitHub. It's open source, so you get every update and bug fix by pulling the latest main. For direct support, reach out via email.
